title: PPF vs SIPs: Long-Term Corpus for ₹2,000/Month
description: The Public Provident Fund (PPF) offers guaranteed, tax-free returns, making it a safe debt instrument for long-term savings. Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs.

faq.q: What is the minimum and maximum investment limit for PPF?
faq.a: You can invest a minimum of ₹500 and a maximum of ₹1.5 lakhs in a financial year into a PPF account. This limit includes both lump-sum and monthly contributions.

faq.q: Are returns from equity SIPs guaranteed?
faq.a: No, returns from equity SIPs are not guaranteed as they are market-linked. The value of your investment can fluctuate based on stock market performance, offering potential for high returns but also carrying risk.

faq.q: Can I invest in both PPF and SIPs simultaneously?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. Many financial planners recommend a diversified approach, combining the safety and tax benefits of PPF with the growth potential of equity SIPs to achieve a balanced portfolio.

faq.q: How is the interest calculated in a PPF account?
faq.a: PPF interest is calculated monthly on the lowest balance between the 5th and the last day of the month. However, it is credited to the account only at the end of each financial year and compounded annually.

faq.q: What is rupee-cost averaging in SIPs?
faq.a: Rupee-cost averaging is an investment strategy where you invest a fixed amount regularly. This means you buy more units when the market price is low and fewer units when the price is high, averaging out your purchase cost over time and potentially reducing risk.

faq.q: What are the tax implications if I withdraw from an equity SIP after 2 years?
faq.a: If you withdraw from an equity SIP after holding the units for more than 1 year, it's considered a Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG). LTCG up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year is tax-exempt; beyond that, it's taxed at 10% without indexation.

faq.q: Can I transfer my PPF account from one bank to another?
faq.a: Yes, you can transfer your PPF account from one bank or post office to another. The process usually involves submitting a request to your existing bank/post office.
